text_blocks.snippet: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common type of skin cancer, arising from abnormal growth of basal cells in the epidermis, the outer layer of skin. It typically appears on sun-exposed areas like the face, neck, and ears, often as a shiny bump, red patch, or scar-like area. While BCC rarely spreads to other parts of the body, it can cause local tissue damage if left untreated.
snippet_highlighted_words: the most common type of skin cancer, arising from abnormal growth of basal cells in the epidermis, the outer layer of skin

list.snippet: Sun Exposure: UV radiation from the sun is the primary cause, damaging DNA in basal cells and leading to uncontrolled growth.
Fair Skin: Individuals with fair skin, light-colored eyes, and a tendency to burn easily are at higher risk.
